day: Thursday of week 23 in Ordinary Time
text:
When we know the right thing to do, we can grow proud of that knowledge. Paul reminds us that knowing better is not the same as loving better. His wrestling with food sacrificed to idols is not really about the food at all—it is about whether we will use our understanding to build ourselves up or to protect someone whose faith is still finding its way. He chooses to set aside his own freedom for the sake of a brother's conscience.

Then Jesus teaches us to love those who oppose us, to give without keeping score, to forgive before being asked. This is not a strategy that makes worldly sense. But it mirrors something true about God himself: he is kind even to the ungrateful and the wicked. When we act this way, we become like our Father. We stop measuring out love in careful portions and begin to pour it out freely, the way God does.

Perhaps today we might notice where we are tempted to stand on what we know is right, forgetting that love might ask us to stand with someone else instead. There is wisdom in knowing when to give up our small certainties for the sake of tenderness toward another soul.
